content_html:
Call4Agents makes the actions of a Python agent safe to retry. You add it to the agent you already have: LangGraph, Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, an MCP server, or plain Python. It does not replace any of them.

Write-up, 5 November 2026: A "yes" is not exactly-once. One approved payment, a crash right after it, a documented resume: 2 payments in LangGraph, Pydantic AI and the OpenAI Agents SDK. Script and every run's data included.

Does your agent repeat an action after a crash? This kills it at every step, restarts it, and tells you which action ran twice. Your agent does not need to use our guard first.

pip install call4agents
call4agents crashtest --demo          # a small agent, without and with the one-line fix
call4agents crashtest your_agent.py   # yours (experimental; every action really runs, so use test accounts)

Then the kit makes it stop:

  • Once-only actions. A crash, a retry or a resume does not send the same email or payment twice.
  • Approvals bound to exact arguments. A "yes" to pay(10, alice) cannot run pay(9999, mallory). A "yes" covers one action, and a later "no" is enforced.
  • Undo. Register how to reverse an action (undo=), and c4a.undo() reverses a run newest first, each undo once only, even across crashes.
  • Idempotency keys for outside APIs. The same key across crashes and resumes, so the payment API itself can drop the duplicate.
  • Record, replay, diff. Rerun a recorded run offline with zero model calls, and find the step where two runs (for example two models) begin to differ.

Version 0.6, early. Standard library only, zero dependencies (PostgreSQL for several machines is an optional extra). Apache-2.0.

# pip install call4agents
import call4agents as c4a

c4a.init(".c4a/first.sqlite")

@c4a.effect(approval=True)
def pay(amount, to):
    print(f"paying {amount} to {to}")
    return "paid"

with c4a.run("order-42"):
    c4a.approve(pay, amount=10, to="alice")   # the person said yes to this exact call
    print(pay(10, "alice"))                    # runs
    print(pay(10, "alice"))                    # a retry: recorded result, no second payment
    pay(9999, "mallory")                       # not approved: raises, nothing is paid
paying 10 to alice
paid
paid
call4agents.ApprovalRequired: __main__.pay needs approval for exactly {"amount":9999,"to":"mallory"}

Run it a second time: pay prints nothing, because the record already holds the result.

Guides with runnable code for each framework: salahmakboul.github.io/call4agents/guides.

Linux (GitHub ubuntu-latest) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓

With the real frameworks, on all three systems with Python 3.12: LangGraph (+ LangChain), Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK and the MCP Python SDK. CI installs the latest release of each, and each run prints the exact versions with call4agents doctor.

See three incidents in five seconds

pip install call4agents
call4agents incident

Each incident runs in real processes with real crashes, once without the kit and once with it. The bank and the agent loop are small local stand-ins; call4agents quickstart below shows the crash in the real frameworks.

Try it (under a minute, offline, no API keys)

pip install call4agents
call4agents quickstart

quickstart runs a plain-Python demo. Then, for each of LangGraph, Pydantic AI and the OpenAI Agents SDK that is installed, it runs a real crash and resume in that framework, using a fake model. Each framework is run once without Call4Agents and once with it. Output on our machine (Windows 10, Python 3.12, all three installed):

Plain Python - crash right after an email is sent, then resume:

  with the run record (crash after the tool)    emails sent: 1
  with the run record (crash inside the tool)   emails sent: 1 (refused to resend: in doubt)
  "yes" to pay(10, alice), call changed to pay(9999, mallory): REFUSED; approved call: PAID; payments: 1

Frameworks found: LangGraph, Pydantic AI, OpenAI Agents SDK

  Pydantic AI        crash after the email, resume:  without call4agents 2 emails,  with call4agents 1
  OpenAI Agents SDK  crash after the email, resume:  without call4agents 2 emails,  with call4agents 1

With no framework installed, only the plain-Python part runs (about 5 seconds on our machine). To see the framework rows, install them first: pip install langgraph langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite pydantic-ai openai-agents (about 75 seconds in a fresh virtual environment).

call4agents selftest checks the demo results. Run it from the root of a repository checkout to run the full offline suites instead (kit, production, stress and idempotency checks).

Found a problem, or something missing? call4agents report prints your system and framework versions and a link to the issue form with them filled in. It sends nothing and opens nothing: you read it and decide. There is no tracking of any kind.

When you need it

  • Your agent sends emails, payments, tickets or database writes, and a crash, a timeout retry or a resume from a checkpoint can repeat them.
  • A person approves an action, and the arguments can change before it runs, for example through an edited saved state or a model asked again after a restart.
  • A person double-clicks "approve", or two workers pick up the same approved task.
  • You call an API that supports Idempotency-Key (Stripe, Adyen and others) and want a crash half-way through to be retried safely instead of needing a person.
  • You switch model or provider and want to see which tool calls changed before you release.

You probably do not need it if your agent only reads data, or if every action already runs inside a durable workflow engine that gives you these guarantees.

How to use it

import call4agents as c4a

c4a.init()                                     # creates .c4a/ledger.sqlite and .c4a/secret

@c4a.effect                                    # once per (run, tool, exact arguments)
def send_email(to, body): ...

@c4a.effect(approval=True)                     # also needs a "yes" for these exact arguments
def pay(amount, to): ...

@c4a.effect(idempotent_for=24 * 3600)          # the API remembers keys for 24 h (Stripe v1)
def charge(amount, to):
    return requests.post(URL, json={"amount": amount, "to": to},
                         headers=c4a.idempotency_headers()).json()

@c4a.recorded                                  # model calls, for replay and diff
def ask_model(prompt): ...

with c4a.run("thread-42"):                     # use the id your framework resumes with
    send_email("bob", "hi")
    send_email("bob", "hi")                    # same action: returns the recorded result, sends nothing
    send_email("bob", "hi", c4a_key="second")  # a deliberate second identical action
    c4a.approve(pay, amount=10, to="alice")    # when the person says yes to what they SAW
    pay(amount=10, to="alice")

Rules worth knowing before you start:

  • Always inside c4a.run(...). An action or approval outside a run raises RuntimeError. New threads do not inherit the run, so enter c4a.run in the thread (or use contextvars.copy_context().run).
  • A tool is identified by module + function name (billing.charge). If you move or rename the function between deploys, a resumed run sees a new tool. Give long-lived tools a fixed name="charge".
  • Arguments need a stable text form: numbers, strings, lists, dicts, sets, dataclasses, Pydantic models. An object that prints its memory address raises TypeError; pass c4a_key= instead. For methods, self is not part of the key.
  • If the function raises, the action may or may not have happened (a timeout after the charge raises too). The next call raises EffectInDoubt and names the error. List errors that prove nothing happened with retry_on=(ConnectionRefusedError,); after those, the next call runs the action again.

LangGraph and LangChain.

  • from call4agents.adapters import langgraph as c4a_lg.
  • Use @c4a_lg.effect in nodes or tools.
  • Call c4a_lg.approve(tool, config, **shown_args) when an interrupt is answered, or c4a_lg.deny(...).
  • The thread id becomes the run id.

Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP. Each has an adapter. It leaves the framework's context argument (RunContext, RunContextWrapper, MCP's Context) out of the key, because that object changes on every call and plain @c4a.effect refuses it. It also finds the run id for you. The framework's own decorator goes on top:

from call4agents.adapters import pydantic_ai as c4a_pai      # run id: the run's conversation_id
@agent.tool
@c4a_pai.effect
def send_email(ctx: RunContext[Deps], to: str, body: str) -> str: ...

from call4agents.adapters import openai_agents as c4a_oa     # run id: c4a.run(...) or your context's session_id
@function_tool
@c4a_oa.effect
def send_email(ctx: RunContextWrapper[dict], to: str, body: str) -> str: ...

from call4agents.adapters import mcp as c4a_mcp              # run id: the Mcp-Session-Id, or run=lambda ctx: ...
@server.tool()
@c4a_mcp.effect
def create_ticket(title: str, ctx: Context) -> str: ...

Each has a copy-and-run example (fake model, no key), tested in CI with the real framework. Each one prints 1 where the same code without the kit prints 2:

python -m call4agents.examples.pydantic_ai_tool     # pip install pydantic-ai
python -m call4agents.examples.openai_agents_tool   # pip install openai-agents
python -m call4agents.examples.mcp_tool             # pip install mcp

Plain Python. Decorate the function with @c4a.effect and wrap the work in c4a.run(<id>).

Undo a run. Register how to reverse each action, then reverse a whole run, newest first:

@c4a.effect(undo=lambda amount, to, result: refunds.create(charge=result["id"]))
def charge(amount, to): ...

@c4a.effect(undo=lambda day: hotel.cancel(day))
def book(day): ...

with c4a.run("trip-42"):
    c4a.undo()          # cancel the booking, then refund the charge; each undo runs once only

Each undo is itself a once-only action. If the process dies half-way, calling c4a.undo() again continues where it stopped. An undo that crashed or raised is "in doubt": undo stops there, and nothing older is touched until a person checks and runs call4agents resolve. Actions without undo= are listed in the result, never skipped silently.

How it works

The kit's whole state is one local SQLite file, which we call the run record. Entries are only ever added to it, never changed or deleted.

  1. Before a decorated action runs, an intent is written: run id, tool name, and a hash of the exact arguments. A unique index lets only one caller write the intent for the same action, so simultaneous callers cannot both start it.
  2. After it returns, the result is written. A later call of the same action gets that result back and the action does not run again.
  3. If the process dies between the two writes, nobody knows whether the action happened. The kit raises EffectInDoubt instead of guessing. You can resolve it in two ways:
    • reconcile= asks the outside system whether the action happened;
    • idempotent_for= lets the kit resend it with the same key while the API still remembers that key (docs/IDEMPOTENCY.md).
  4. Approvals. An approval is an HMAC, made with a local secret, over the tool name and its exact arguments, and it is scoped to the run. Each approval can be spent by one action only. A later deny cancels it.
  5. Replay. c4a.init(replay_from="old.sqlite") returns recorded model calls and results without calling anything. They come back as the same Python types, including Pydantic models and dataclasses. call4agents diff a.sqlite b.sqlite shows the step where two runs start to differ.

python -m call4agents ... works the same way. <record> is a file, or a postgresql:// address for a shared record.

Test your own agent (experimental)

call4agents crashtest your_agent.py runs your script in a new empty folder, once cleanly, then once per crash point. It kills the process just before and just after each action, and just before each write saved to SQLite or to a file in that folder. Then it starts the script again and compares what ran with the clean run:

  • RAN TWICE: the same call ran more times than in the clean run.
  • NOT APPROVED: a call the clean run never made. On a restart the environment has CRASHTEST_RESUME=1, so your script can act out a changed call.
  • NEVER FINISHED: the call was lost, or the framework hid an in-doubt stop.

Your script must be able to restart: a fixed run or thread id, and saved state in the current folder. Actions are found by reading the script (names like pay or send_email, and calls that post, delete or run commands). Add your own with --watch name,name. Every action really runs, many times, with your environment: use test accounts.

It does not see writes to PostgreSQL, Redis or a remote service as crash points, and it tests only the path your script takes. A clean result covers that path and those crash points, nothing more.

call4agents scan <path> reads Python source and runs nothing. It lists functions given to a model as tools whose code sends, pays, deletes or writes, with no approval or once-only guard on them. It cannot see a guard in another file or service, tools built at runtime, or what a call does past one helper in the same file. Measured results are in docs/SCAN_RESULTS.md.

Audit export (experimental)

call4agents audit <record> out.json writes who approved what, when, for which exact arguments, and what ran. It uses the record's secret (C4A_SECRET or its secret file) and never creates one. call4agents audit-verify out.json fails if any value was changed or any entry was removed, added or moved.

Limits: anyone with the secret can sign a false export, so this shows the file has not changed since a holder of the secret signed it. It does not show that the record was honest before the export, and it is not proof for an outside party. A name appears only where one was recorded (c4a.decide(ticket, "approve", by="sam")). Action results are left out, but arguments are included, so treat the file as sensitive.

In production

Approval tickets (experimental, new in 0.4; all three frameworks in 0.5)

When your agent pauses for a person and resumes later, the approval travels through a UI, a queue or a saved state. Tickets make sure the "yes" that comes back belongs to a pause your server really made, for the exact call the person saw:

with c4a.run("order-42"):
    ticket = c4a.pause(pay, amount=10, to="alice")   # recorded; show the ticket with the call
# ... later, when the person answers (any process that opens the same record):
c4a.decide(ticket, "approve", by="sam")              # or "deny"

The ticket holds no arguments, only a random id and a signature. decide reads the call from the record, so nothing the client sends back can change what runs. A ticket the record did not issue, or one that was changed, expired or already decided, raises TicketRefused. The decision is stored with who made it. The action still runs only if it is called with the approved arguments, so a "deny" holds even if a framework runs the tool anyway.

With Pydantic AI (requires_approval=True tools):

from call4agents.adapters import pydantic_ai as c4a_pai

@agent.tool(requires_approval=True)
@c4a_pai.effect(approval=True)
def pay(ctx: RunContext, amount: int, to: str) -> str: ...

result = agent.run_sync("pay alice 10", conversation_id="order-42")   # ends with DeferredToolRequests
tickets = c4a_pai.tickets(result, [pay])                  # {tool_call_id: ticket}: show each with its call
results = c4a_pai.results({ticket: "approve"}, by="sam")  # the person's answers -> DeferredToolResults
agent.run_sync(message_history=result.all_messages(), deferred_tool_results=results,
               conversation_id="order-42")

With the OpenAI Agents SDK (needs_approval=True tools):

from call4agents.adapters import openai_agents as c4a_oa

pay_fn = c4a_oa.effect(pay, approval=True)                  # keep this one: tickets() needs it
agent = Agent(name="payer", tools=[function_tool(pay_fn, needs_approval=True)], ...)

result = await Runner.run(agent, "pay alice 10", context={"session_id": "order-42"})
tickets = c4a_oa.tickets(result, [pay_fn])                  # {call_id: ticket}
state = c4a_oa.apply(result.to_state(), {ticket: "approve"}, by="sam")   # state.approve / state.reject
await Runner.run(agent, state)

With LangGraph (the ticket goes in the interrupt; a node that re-runs on resume gets the same ticket back):

from call4agents.adapters import langgraph as c4a_lg

def ask(state, config):
    ticket = c4a_lg.pause(pay, config, **state["call"])
    interrupt({"call": state["call"], "ticket": ticket})

# when the person answers:
c4a.decide(ticket, "approve", by="sam")
graph.invoke(Command(resume="decided"), config)

Checks T1-T13 (python -m tests.test_tickets) cover a forged or edited ticket, a pause edited in the record, a ticket from another record, a second decision, expiry, a denied call that the framework runs anyway, and a call with other arguments than the approved ones. With the real frameworks they cover, for each of Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK and LangGraph: the approved call runs once, a denied call does not run, and a call that the client or the saved state changed after the pause does not run. (In the OpenAI Agents SDK, changed arguments under the same call id are already refused by the SDK itself; the check also covers a call replaced with a new id, which only the ticket catches.) Experimental: no real user has tried it yet, and the API may change.

When something goes wrong

You see What it means What to do
ApprovalRequired no unused "yes" for exactly these arguments (or a later "no") ask the person, then c4a.approve(...) or c4a.decide(ticket, ...)
EffectInDoubt the process stopped during the action; nobody knows if it happened get an authoritative answer from the provider (a read that finds nothing can lag), then call4agents resolve <record> <key> done|not-done "what you checked"
TicketRefused the ticket was not issued here, or was changed, expired or already decided pause again to ask the person again
KeyConflict a c4a_key (or key=) that already names one call was used with arguments that mean something else; nothing ran use a new key for a different action
LedgerError the record cannot be used safely (wrong file, newer format, network drive, missing secret) the message says which; docs/PRODUCTION.md lists every message

Still stuck? call4agents report prints your versions and a link to the issue form. It sends nothing.

Several machines (beta, new in 0.3)

Beta. Tested with separate processes and one local PostgreSQL server on Linux, macOS and Windows. Not yet used on real networks or in production; the options may still change.

When workers or replicas on different machines can pick up the same run, they need one shared record. Point every machine at the same PostgreSQL database and give them the same secret:

# pip install "call4agents[postgres]"
c4a.init("postgresql://user:password@db-host/agents", secret=os.environ["C4A_SECRET"].encode())

The table and the UNIQUE indexes are the same as in the SQLite file, so the same guarantees hold across machines. This covers the case in langgraph#7417, where a long tool call is sent to a second worker while the first is still running it. The second worker gets EffectInDoubt instead of running the call again, and a later caller gets the recorded result. The secret has to be passed in, because a local secret file would be different on each machine. The on-call commands take the address instead of a file: call4agents doubt postgresql://db-host/agents. Put the password in PGPASSWORD, not in the address, because command lines can be seen by other users. archive copies finished runs to a SQLite file and then removes them from the database. A crash between the two steps leaves those runs in both places; nothing is lost.

What is proven and what is not

Proven by tests in this repository (tests/):

  • the table above;
  • the big test (python -m tests.bigtest_c4a). 12 processes are killed at random while they charge 300 orders through a payment API that drops and delays answers. The result is 0 double charges. Without the kit, the same run charges 244 of 300 orders twice or more;
  • an action resumed in 3 new processes, as a method with a set argument, runs once;
  • a real process killed before and after every write to the record and inside the action, then the recovery killed too (python -m tests.test_crash_matrix, 412 crashes): no double charge and no unapproved payment;
  • call4agents crashtest finds the repeat in a small real agent on LangGraph, Pydantic AI and the OpenAI Agents SDK, and finds none with the guard (python -m tests.test_crashtest --require-frameworks); with our old approval bypass put back, its check fails;
  • 14 simultaneous callers of one action: it runs once;
  • 8 simultaneous actions on one "yes": exactly one runs;
  • 3,000 of 3,000 records from 20 parallel writers;
  • 5 kills during writes left the file intact;
  • a crash after a payment API charged, then a resume with the idempotency key: 1 charge, and the original charge is returned;
  • replay returns the same types, including real Pydantic and OpenAI SDK objects;
  • a shared PostgreSQL record (python -m tests.test_shared_record), with each machine played by a separate process: 8 machines call one action at once and it runs once; a long action still running on one machine is not started again by a second one; after a crash on one machine, the next raises EffectInDoubt; a "yes" given on one machine counts on another, only for the same arguments and the same secret.

Each guard is mutation-tested: when its bug is put back, its check fails. A no-op control is run next to every batch of mutations. Rerun them with python -m tests.mutations.run_kit_mutations.

Not proven:

  • real payment or email systems, and production traffic;
  • systems and Python versions not listed at the top of this page;
  • several real machines on a real network sharing one PostgreSQL record (the tests use separate processes and one local PostgreSQL server), and managed platforms such as LangGraph Cloud;
  • an independent code review (see docs/REVIEWED.md);
  • crashtest and scan on real production agents;
  • frameworks other than the four with adapters (LangGraph, Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP); the decorator itself works in any framework;
  • approval tickets with real users and real approval UIs (experimental: tested with fake models only).

Costs and limits

  • A crash during an action is not resolved for you. You get EffectInDoubt unless you use reconcile= or idempotent_for=. Most frameworks would simply run the action again.
  • A refused approval means the action does not run. Your app has to ask the person again.
  • You decorate each action yourself, and call approve with the arguments the person saw.
  • Replaying a recorded run that contains approval-gated actions needs the approvals again in the new run record (c4a.approve(...) before the replayed call).
  • If the model rewrites the arguments on a retry (10 becomes 10.00), the call is treated as a new action. Pass c4a_key= (for example, an order id) when that can happen. A key names one action: calling it again with arguments that mean something else raises KeyConflict and nothing runs (numbers are compared by value, so 10, 10.0 and Decimal("10.00") are the same amount).
  • The secret in .c4a/secret protects approvals from anyone who cannot read that file. It does not protect them from someone who can (see docs/THREAT_MODEL.md).

When you need it Your agent sends emails, payments, tickets or database writes, and a crash, a timeout retry or a resume from a checkpoint can repeat them. A person approves an action, and the arguments can change before it runs, for example through an edited saved state or a model asked again after a restart. A person double-clicks "approve", or two workers pick up the same approved task. You call an API that supports Idempotency-Key (Stripe, Adyen and others) and want a crash half-way through to be retried safely instead of needing a person. You switch model or provider and want to see which tool calls changed before you release. You probably do not need it if your agent only reads data, or if every action already runs inside a durable workflow engine that gives you these guarantees. How to use it import call4agents as c4a c4a.init() # creates .c4a/ledger.sqlite and .c4a/secret @c4a.effect # once per (run, tool, exact arguments) def send_email(to, body): ... @c4a.effect(approval=True) # also needs a "yes" for these exact arguments def pay(amount, to): ... @c4a.effect(idempotent_for=24 * 3600) # the API remembers keys for 24 h (Stripe v1) def charge(amount, to): return requests.post(URL, json={"amount": amount, "to": to}, headers=c4a.idempotency_headers()).json() @c4a.recorded # model calls, for replay and diff def ask_model(prompt): ... with c4a.run("thread-42"): # use the id your framework resumes with send_email("bob", "hi") send_email("bob", "hi") # same action: returns the recorded result, sends nothing send_email("bob", "hi", c4a_key="second") # a deliberate second identical action c4a.approve(pay, amount=10, to="alice") # when the person says yes to what they SAW pay(amount=10, to="alice") Rules worth knowing before you start: Always inside c4a.run(...). An action or approval outside a run raises RuntimeError. New threads do not inherit the run, so enter c4a.run in the thread (or use contextvars.copy_context().run). A tool is identified by module + function name (billing.charge). If you move or rename the function between deploys, a resumed run sees a new tool. Give long-lived tools a fixed name="charge". Arguments need a stable text form: numbers, strings, lists, dicts, sets, dataclasses, Pydantic models. An object that prints its memory address raises TypeError; pass c4a_key= instead. For methods, self is not part of the key. If the function raises, the action may or may not have happened (a timeout after the charge raises too). The next call raises EffectInDoubt and names the error. List errors that prove nothing happened with retry_on=(ConnectionRefusedError,); after those, the next call runs the action again. LangGraph and LangChain. from call4agents.adapters import langgraph as c4a_lg. Use @c4a_lg.effect in nodes or tools. Call c4a_lg.approve(tool, config, **shown_args) when an interrupt is answered, or c4a_lg.deny(...). The thread id becomes the run id. Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP. Each has an adapter. It leaves the framework's context argument (RunContext, RunContextWrapper, MCP's Context) out of the key, because that object changes on every call and plain @c4a.effect refuses it. It also finds the run id for you. The framework's own decorator goes on top: from call4agents.adapters import pydantic_ai as c4a_pai # run id: the run's conversation_id @agent.tool @c4a_pai.effect def send_email(ctx: RunContext[Deps], to: str, body: str) -> str: ... from call4agents.adapters import openai_agents as c4a_oa # run id: c4a.run(...) or your context's session_id @function_tool @c4a_oa.effect def send_email(ctx: RunContextWrapper[dict], to: str, body: str) -> str: ... from call4agents.adapters import mcp as c4a_mcp # run id: the Mcp-Session-Id, or run=lambda ctx: ... @server.tool() @c4a_mcp.effect def create_ticket(title: str, ctx: Context) -> str: ... Each has a copy-and-run example (fake model, no key), tested in CI with the real framework. Each one prints 1 where the same code without the kit prints 2: python -m call4agents.examples.pydantic_ai_tool # pip install pydantic-ai python -m call4agents.examples.openai_agents_tool # pip install openai-agents python -m call4agents.examples.mcp_tool # pip install mcp Plain Python. Decorate the function with @c4a.effect and wrap the work in c4a.run(<id>). Undo a run. Register how to reverse each action, then reverse a whole run, newest first: @c4a.effect(undo=lambda amount, to, result: refunds.create(charge=result["id"])) def charge(amount, to): ... @c4a.effect(undo=lambda day: hotel.cancel(day)) def book(day): ... with c4a.run("trip-42"): c4a.undo() # cancel the booking, then refund the charge; each undo runs once only Each undo is itself a once-only action. If the process dies half-way, calling c4a.undo() again continues where it stopped. An undo that crashed or raised is "in doubt": undo stops there, and nothing older is touched until a person checks and runs call4agents resolve. Actions without undo= are listed in the result, never skipped silently. How it works The kit's whole state is one local SQLite file, which we call the run record. Entries are only ever added to it, never changed or deleted. Before a decorated action runs, an intent is written: run id, tool name, and a hash of the exact arguments. A unique index lets only one caller write the intent for the same action, so simultaneous callers cannot both start it. After it returns, the result is written. A later call of the same action gets that result back and the action does not run again. If the process dies between the two writes, nobody knows whether the action happened. The kit raises EffectInDoubt instead of guessing. You can resolve it in two ways: reconcile= asks the outside system whether the action happened; idempotent_for= lets the kit resend it with the same key while the API still remembers that key (docs/IDEMPOTENCY.md). Approvals. An approval is an HMAC, made with a local secret, over the tool name and its exact arguments, and it is scoped to the run. Each approval can be spent by one action only. A later deny cancels it. Replay. c4a.init(replay_from="old.sqlite") returns recorded model calls and results without calling anything. They come back as the same Python types, including Pydantic models and dataclasses. call4agents diff a.sqlite b.sqlite shows the step where two runs start to differ. Commands Command What it does call4agents quickstart the demo plus a crash and resume in each installed framework call4agents incident three approval incidents, without and with the kit call4agents crashtest <script> kills your agent at every step, restarts it, reports what ran twice or without approval (experimental) call4agents scan <path> lists tools that send, pay, delete or write with no approval or once-only guard; runs nothing (experimental) call4agents audit <record> <out.json> [--run id] a signed export: who approved what, when, for which arguments, and what ran (experimental) call4agents audit-verify <out.json> exit 0 only if nothing in the export was changed call4agents demo the plain-Python demo only call4agents selftest the kit's checks (in a repository checkout, the full offline suites) call4agents doctor system and framework versions for a bug report; prints only, sends nothing call4agents report the same, plus a link to the issue form with it filled in; prints only, sends nothing call4agents status <record> rows, actions, actions in doubt, integrity call4agents doubt <record> [--fail-if-any] every action that may or may not have happened (exit 3 if any, for alerts) call4agents resolve <record> <key> done|not-done "note" decide one in-doubt action; stored as a new row with your note call4agents archive <record> <archive> <days> move finished runs older than N days to another file call4agents verify <record> integrity, format version, late results call4agents diff a.sqlite b.sqlite [run_id] the step where two recorded runs start to differ call4agents prove spec.json puts each bug back and checks that your guard catches it python -m call4agents ... works the same way. <record> is a file, or a postgresql:// address for a shared record. Test your own agent (experimental) call4agents crashtest your_agent.py runs your script in a new empty folder, once cleanly, then once per crash point. It kills the process just before and just after each action, and just before each write saved to SQLite or to a file in that folder. Then it starts the script again and compares what ran with the clean run: RAN TWICE: the same call ran more times than in the clean run. NOT APPROVED: a call the clean run never made. On a restart the environment has CRASHTEST_RESUME=1, so your script can act out a changed call. NEVER FINISHED: the call was lost, or the framework hid an in-doubt stop. Your script must be able to restart: a fixed run or thread id, and saved state in the current folder. Actions are found by reading the script (names like pay or send_email, and calls that post, delete or run commands). Add your own with --watch name,name. Every action really runs, many times, with your environment: use test accounts. It does not see writes to PostgreSQL, Redis or a remote service as crash points, and it tests only the path your script takes. A clean result covers that path and those crash points, nothing more. call4agents scan <path> reads Python source and runs nothing. It lists functions given to a model as tools whose code sends, pays, deletes or writes, with no approval or once-only guard on them. It cannot see a guard in another file or service, tools built at runtime, or what a call does past one helper in the same file. Measured results are in docs/SCAN_RESULTS.md. Audit export (experimental) call4agents audit <record> out.json writes who approved what, when, for which exact arguments, and what ran. It uses the record's secret (C4A_SECRET or its secret file) and never creates one. call4agents audit-verify out.json fails if any value was changed or any entry was removed, added or moved. Limits: anyone with the secret can sign a false export, so this shows the file has not changed since a holder of the secret signed it. It does not show that the record was honest before the export, and it is not proof for an outside party. A name appears only where one was recorded (c4a.decide(ticket, "approve", by="sam")). Action results are left out, but arguments are included, so treat the file as sensitive. In production docs/PRODUCTION.md covers the rest: costs: a new action is 1.9 ms (median) on our machine, a repeated one 45 µs; the big test, with 12 processes, random kills and a payment API that drops answers: 0 double charges, against 244 of 300 orders without the kit; secret rotation, archiving, what the record stores, every error message and what to do; a guide for whoever is on call. Approval tickets (experimental, new in 0.4; all three frameworks in 0.5) When your agent pauses for a person and resumes later, the approval travels through a UI, a queue or a saved state. Tickets make sure the "yes" that comes back belongs to a pause your server really made, for the exact call the person saw: with c4a.run("order-42"): ticket = c4a.pause(pay, amount=10, to="alice") # recorded; show the ticket with the call # ... later, when the person answers (any process that opens the same record): c4a.decide(ticket, "approve", by="sam") # or "deny" The ticket holds no arguments, only a random id and a signature. decide reads the call from the record, so nothing the client sends back can change what runs. A ticket the record did not issue, or one that was changed, expired or already decided, raises TicketRefused. The decision is stored with who made it. The action still runs only if it is called with the approved arguments, so a "deny" holds even if a framework runs the tool anyway. With Pydantic AI (requires_approval=True tools): from call4agents.adapters import pydantic_ai as c4a_pai @agent.tool(requires_approval=True) @c4a_pai.effect(approval=True) def pay(ctx: RunContext, amount: int, to: str) -> str: ... result = agent.run_sync("pay alice 10", conversation_id="order-42") # ends with DeferredToolRequests tickets = c4a_pai.tickets(result, [pay]) # {tool_call_id: ticket}: show each with its call results = c4a_pai.results({ticket: "approve"}, by="sam") # the person's answers -> DeferredToolResults agent.run_sync(message_history=result.all_messages(), deferred_tool_results=results, conversation_id="order-42") With the OpenAI Agents SDK (needs_approval=True tools): from call4agents.adapters import openai_agents as c4a_oa pay_fn = c4a_oa.effect(pay, approval=True) # keep this one: tickets() needs it agent = Agent(name="payer", tools=[function_tool(pay_fn, needs_approval=True)], ...) result = await Runner.run(agent, "pay alice 10", context={"session_id": "order-42"}) tickets = c4a_oa.tickets(result, [pay_fn]) # {call_id: ticket} state = c4a_oa.apply(result.to_state(), {ticket: "approve"}, by="sam") # state.approve / state.reject await Runner.run(agent, state) With LangGraph (the ticket goes in the interrupt; a node that re-runs on resume gets the same ticket back): from call4agents.adapters import langgraph as c4a_lg def ask(state, config): ticket = c4a_lg.pause(pay, config, **state["call"]) interrupt({"call": state["call"], "ticket": ticket}) # when the person answers: c4a.decide(ticket, "approve", by="sam") graph.invoke(Command(resume="decided"), config) Checks T1-T13 (python -m tests.test_tickets) cover a forged or edited ticket, a pause edited in the record, a ticket from another record, a second decision, expiry, a denied call that the framework runs anyway, and a call with other arguments than the approved ones. With the real frameworks they cover, for each of Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK and LangGraph: the approved call runs once, a denied call does not run, and a call that the client or the saved state changed after the pause does not run. (In the OpenAI Agents SDK, changed arguments under the same call id are already refused by the SDK itself; the check also covers a call replaced with a new id, which only the ticket catches.) When something goes wrong You see What it means What to do ApprovalRequired no unused "yes" for exactly these arguments (or a later "no") ask the person, then c4a.approve(...) or c4a.decide(ticket, ...) EffectInDoubt the process stopped during the action; nobody knows if it happened get an authoritative answer from the provider (a read that finds nothing can lag), then call4agents resolve <record> <key> done|not-done "what you checked" TicketRefused the ticket was not issued here, or was changed, expired or already decided pause again to ask the person again KeyConflict a c4a_key (or key=) that already names one call was used with arguments that mean something else; nothing ran use a new key for a different action LedgerError the record cannot be used safely (wrong file, newer format, network drive, missing secret) the message says which; docs/PRODUCTION.md lists every message Still stuck? call4agents report prints your versions and a link to the issue form. It sends nothing. Several machines (beta, new in 0.3) Beta. Tested with separate processes and one local PostgreSQL server on Linux, macOS and Windows. Not yet used on real networks or in production; the options may still change. When workers or replicas on different machines can pick up the same run, they need one shared record. Point every machine at the same PostgreSQL database and give them the same secret: # pip install "call4agents[postgres]" c4a.init("postgresql://user:password@db-host/agents", secret=os.environ["C4A_SECRET"].encode()) The table and the UNIQUE indexes are the same as in the SQLite file, so the same guarantees hold across machines. This covers the case in langgraph#7417, where a long tool call is sent to a second worker while the first is still running it. The second worker gets EffectInDoubt instead of running the call again, and a later caller gets the recorded result. The secret has to be passed in, because a local secret file would be different on each machine. The on-call commands take the address instead of a file: call4agents doubt postgresql://db-host/agents. Put the password in PGPASSWORD, not in the address, because command lines can be seen by other users. archive copies finished runs to a SQLite file and then removes them from the database. A crash between the two steps leaves those runs in both places; nothing is lost. Measured in each framework You can rerun every number in this table. What is proven and what is not Proven by tests in this repository (tests/): the table above; the big test (python -m tests.bigtest_c4a). 12 processes are killed at random while they charge 300 orders through a payment API that drops and delays answers. The result is 0 double charges. Without the kit, the same run charges 244 of 300 orders twice or more; an action resumed in 3 new processes, as a method with a set argument, runs once; a real process killed before and after every write to the record and inside the action, then the recovery killed too (python -m tests.test_crash_matrix, 412 crashes): no double charge and no unapproved payment; call4agents crashtest finds the repeat in a small real agent on LangGraph, Pydantic AI and the OpenAI Agents SDK, and finds none with the guard (python -m tests.test_crashtest --require-frameworks); with our old approval bypass put back, its check fails; 14 simultaneous callers of one action: it runs once; 8 simultaneous actions on one "yes": exactly one runs; 3,000 of 3,000 records from 20 parallel writers; 5 kills during writes left the file intact; a crash after a payment API charged, then a resume with the idempotency key: 1 charge, and the original charge is returned; replay returns the same types, including real Pydantic and OpenAI SDK objects; a shared PostgreSQL record (python -m tests.test_shared_record), with each machine played by a separate process: 8 machines call one action at once and it runs once; a long action still running on one machine is not started again by a second one; after a crash on one machine, the next raises EffectInDoubt; a "yes" given on one machine counts on another, only for the same arguments and the same secret. Each guard is mutation-tested: when its bug is put back, its check fails. A no-op control is run next to every batch of mutations. Rerun them with python -m tests.mutations.run_kit_mutations. Not proven: real payment or email systems, and production traffic; systems and Python versions not listed at the top of this page; several real machines on a real network sharing one PostgreSQL record (the tests use separate processes and one local PostgreSQL server), and managed platforms such as LangGraph Cloud; an independent code review (see docs/REVIEWED.md); crashtest and scan on real production agents; frameworks other than the four with adapters (LangGraph, Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP); the decorator itself works in any framework; approval tickets with real users and real approval UIs (experimental: tested with fake models only). Costs and limits A crash during an action is not resolved for you. You get EffectInDoubt unless you use reconcile= or idempotent_for=. Most frameworks would simply run the action again. A refused approval means the action does not run. Your app has to ask the person again. You decorate each action yourself, and call approve with the arguments the person saw. Replaying a recorded run that contains approval-gated actions needs the approvals again in the new run record (c4a.approve(...) before the replayed call). If the model rewrites the arguments on a retry (10 becomes 10.00), the call is treated as a new action. Pass c4a_key= (for example, an order id) when that can happen. A key names one action: calling it again with arguments that mean something else raises KeyConflict and nothing runs (numbers are compared by value, so 10, 10.0 and Decimal("10.00") are the same amount). The secret in .c4a/secret protects approvals from anyone who cannot read that file. It does not protect them from someone who can (see docs/THREAT_MODEL.md). content_html_zh:
Call4Agents makes the actions of a Python agent safe to retry. You add it to the agent you already have: LangGraph, Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, an MCP server, or plain Python. It does not replace any of them.

Write-up, 5 November 2026: A "yes" is not exactly-once. One approved payment, a crash right after it, a documented resume: 2 payments in LangGraph, Pydantic AI and the OpenAI Agents SDK. Script and every run's data included.

Does your agent repeat an action after a crash? This kills it at every step, restarts it, and tells you which action ran twice. Your agent does not need to use our guard first.

pip install call4agents
call4agents crashtest --demo          # a small agent, without and with the one-line fix
call4agents crashtest your_agent.py   # yours (experimental; every action really runs, so use test accounts)

Then the kit makes it stop:

  • Once-only actions. A crash, a retry or a resume does not send the same email or payment twice.
  • Approvals bound to exact arguments. A "yes" to pay(10, alice) cannot run pay(9999, mallory). A "yes" covers one action, and a later "no" is enforced.
  • Undo. Register how to reverse an action (undo=), and c4a.undo() reverses a run newest first, each undo once only, even across crashes.
  • Idempotency keys for outside APIs. The same key across crashes and resumes, so the payment API itself can drop the duplicate.
  • Record, replay, diff. Rerun a recorded run offline with zero model calls, and find the step where two runs (for example two models) begin to differ.

Version 0.6, early. Standard library only, zero dependencies (PostgreSQL for several machines is an optional extra). 阿帕奇-2.0。

# pip install call4agents
import call4agents as c4a

c4a.init(".c4a/first.sqlite")

@c4a.effect(approval=True)
def pay(amount, to):
    print(f"paying {amount} to {to}")
    return "paid"

with c4a.run("order-42"):
    c4a.approve(pay, amount=10, to="alice")   # the person said yes to this exact call
    print(pay(10, "alice"))                    # runs
    print(pay(10, "alice"))                    # a retry: recorded result, no second payment
    pay(9999, "mallory")                       # not approved: raises, nothing is paid
paying 10 to alice
paid
paid
call4agents.ApprovalRequired: __main__.pay needs approval for exactly {"amount":9999,"to":"mallory"}

Run it a second time: pay prints nothing, because the record already holds the result.

Each incident runs in real processes with real crashes, once without the kit and once with it. The bank and the agent loop are small local stand-ins; call4agents quickstart below shows the crash in the real frameworks.

Try it (under a minute, offline, no API keys)

Each framework is run once without Call4Agents and once with it. Output on our machine (Windows 10, Python 3.12, all three installed):

With no framework installed, only the plain-Python part runs (about 5 seconds on our machine). To see the framework rows, install them first: pip install langgraph langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite pydantic-ai openai-agents (about 75 seconds in a fresh virtual environment).

call4agents selftest checks the demo results. Run it from the root of a repository checkout to run the full offline suites instead (kit, production, stress and idempotency checks).

Found a problem, or something missing? call4agents report prints your system and framework versions and a link to the issue form with them filled in. It sends nothing and opens nothing: you read it and decide. There is no tracking of any kind.

When you need it

  • Your agent sends emails, payments, tickets or database writes, and a crash, a timeout retry or a resume from a checkpoint can repeat them.
  • A person approves an action, and the arguments can change before it runs, for example through an edited saved state or a model asked again after a restart.
  • A person double-clicks "approve", or two workers pick up the same approved task.
  • You call an API that supports Idempotency-Key (Stripe, Adyen and others) and want a crash half-way through to be retried safely instead of needing a person.
  • You switch model or provider and want to see which tool calls changed before you release.

You probably do not need it if your agent only reads data, or if every action already runs inside a durable workflow engine that gives you these guarantees.

如何使用

import call4agents as c4a

c4a.init()                                     # creates .c4a/ledger.sqlite and .c4a/secret

@c4a.effect                                    # once per (run, tool, exact arguments)
def send_email(to, body): ...

@c4a.effect(approval=True)                     # also needs a "yes" for these exact arguments
def pay(amount, to): ...

@c4a.effect(idempotent_for=24 * 3600)          # the API remembers keys for 24 h (Stripe v1)
def charge(amount, to):
    return requests.post(URL, json={"amount": amount, "to": to},
                         headers=c4a.idempotency_headers()).json()

@c4a.recorded                                  # model calls, for replay and diff
def ask_model(prompt): ...

with c4a.run("thread-42"):                     # use the id your framework resumes with
    send_email("bob", "hi")
    send_email("bob", "hi")                    # same action: returns the recorded result, sends nothing
    send_email("bob", "hi", c4a_key="second")  # a deliberate second identical action
    c4a.approve(pay, amount=10, to="alice")    # when the person says yes to what they SAW
    pay(amount=10, to="alice")

Rules worth knowing before you start:

  • Always inside c4a.run(...). An action or approval outside a run raises RuntimeError. New threads do not inherit the run, so enter c4a.run in the thread (or use contextvars.copy_context().run).
  • A tool is identified by module + function name (billing.charge). If you move or rename the function between deploys, a resumed run sees a new tool. Give long-lived tools a fixed name="charge".
  • Arguments need a stable text form: numbers, strings, lists, dicts, sets, dataclasses, Pydantic models. An object that prints its memory address raises TypeError; pass c4a_key= instead. For methods, self is not part of the key.
  • If the function raises, the action may or may not have happened (a timeout after the charge raises too). The next call raises EffectInDoubt and names the error. List errors that prove nothing happened with retry_on=(ConnectionRefusedError,); after those, the next call runs the action again.

LangGraph and LangChain.

  • from call4agents.adapters import langgraph as c4a_lg.
  • Use @c4a_lg.effect in nodes or tools.
  • Call c4a_lg.approve(tool, config, **shown_args) when an interrupt is answered, or c4a_lg.deny(...).
  • The thread id becomes the run id.

Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP. Each has an adapter. It leaves the framework's context argument (RunContext, RunContextWrapper, MCP's Context) out of the key, because that object changes on every call and plain @c4a.effect refuses it. It also finds the run id for you. The framework's own decorator goes on top:

from call4agents.adapters import pydantic_ai as c4a_pai      # run id: the run's conversation_id
@agent.tool
@c4a_pai.effect
def send_email(ctx: RunContext[Deps], to: str, body: str) -> str: ...

from call4agents.adapters import openai_agents as c4a_oa     # run id: c4a.run(...) or your context's session_id
@function_tool
@c4a_oa.effect
def send_email(ctx: RunContextWrapper[dict], to: str, body: str) -> str: ...

from call4agents.adapters import mcp as c4a_mcp              # run id: the Mcp-Session-Id, or run=lambda ctx: ...
@server.tool()
@c4a_mcp.effect
def create_ticket(title: str, ctx: Context) -> str: ...

Each has a copy-and-run example (fake model, no key), tested in CI with the real framework. Each one prints 1 where the same code without the kit prints 2:

python -m call4agents.examples.pydantic_ai_tool     # pip install pydantic-ai
python -m call4agents.examples.openai_agents_tool   # pip install openai-agents
python -m call4agents.examples.mcp_tool             # pip install mcp

Plain Python. Decorate the function with @c4a.effect and wrap the work in c4a.run(<id>).

Undo a run. Register how to reverse each action, then reverse a whole run, newest first:

@c4a.effect(undo=lambda amount, to, result: refunds.create(charge=result["id"]))
def charge(amount, to): ...

@c4a.effect(undo=lambda day: hotel.cancel(day))
def book(day): ...

with c4a.run("trip-42"):
    c4a.undo()          # cancel the booking, then refund the charge; each undo runs once only

Each undo is itself a once-only action. If the process dies half-way, calling c4a.undo() again continues where it stopped. An undo that crashed or raised is "in doubt": undo stops there, and nothing older is touched until a person checks and runs call4agents resolve. Actions without undo= are listed in the result, never skipped silently.

它是如何运作的

The kit's whole state is one local SQLite file, which we call the run record. Entries are only ever added to it, never changed or deleted.

  1. Before a decorated action runs, an intent is written: run id, tool name, and a hash of the exact arguments. A unique index lets only one caller write the intent for the same action, so simultaneous callers cannot both start it.
  2. After it returns, the result is written. A later call of the same action gets that result back and the action does not run again.
  3. If the process dies between the two writes, nobody knows whether the action happened. The kit raises EffectInDoubt instead of guessing. You can resolve it in two ways: reconcile= asks the outside system whether the action happened; idempotent_for= lets the kit resend it with the same key while the API still remembers that key (docs/IDEMPOTENCY.md).
  4. Approvals. An approval is an HMAC, made with a local secret, over the tool name and its exact arguments, and it is scoped to the run. Each approval can be spent by one action only. A later deny cancels it.
  5. Replay. c4a.init(replay_from="old.sqlite") returns recorded model calls and results without calling anything. They come back as the same Python types, including Pydantic models and dataclasses. call4agents diff a.sqlite b.sqlite shows the step where two runs start to differ.

Test your own agent (experimental)

call4agents crashtest your_agent.py runs your script in a new empty folder, once cleanly, then once per crash point. It kills the process just before and just after each action, and just before each write saved to SQLite or to a file in that folder. Then it starts the script again and compares what ran with the clean run:

  • RAN TWICE: the same call ran more times than in the clean run.
  • NOT APPROVED: a call the clean run never made. On a restart the environment has CRASHTEST_RESUME=1, so your script can act out a changed call.
  • NEVER FINISHED: the call was lost, or the framework hid an in-doubt stop.

Your script must be able to restart: a fixed run or thread id, and saved state in the current folder. Actions are found by reading the script (names like pay or send_email, and calls that post, delete or run commands). Add your own with --watch name,name. Every action really runs, many times, with your environment: use test accounts.

It does not see writes to PostgreSQL, Redis or a remote service as crash points, and it tests only the path your script takes. A clean result covers that path and those crash points, nothing more.

call4agents scan <path> reads Python source and runs nothing. It lists functions given to a model as tools whose code sends, pays, deletes or writes, with no approval or once-only guard on them. It cannot see a guard in another file or service, tools built at runtime, or what a call does past one helper in the same file. Measured results are in docs/SCAN_RESULTS.md.

Audit export (experimental)

call4agents audit <record> out.json writes who approved what, when, for which exact arguments, and what ran. It uses the record's secret (C4A_SECRET or its secret file) and never creates one. call4agents audit-verify out.json fails if any value was changed or any entry was removed, added or moved.

Limits: anyone with the secret can sign a false export, so this shows the file has not changed since a holder of the secret signed it. It does not show that the record was honest before the export, and it is not proof for an outside party. A name appears only where one was recorded (c4a.decide(ticket, "approve", by="sam")). Action results are left out, but arguments are included, so treat the file as sensitive.

Approval tickets (experimental, new in 0.4; all three frameworks in 0.5)

When your agent pauses for a person and resumes later, the approval travels through a UI, a queue or a saved state. Tickets make sure the "yes" that comes back belongs to a pause your server really made, for the exact call the person saw:

with c4a.run("order-42"):
    ticket = c4a.pause(pay, amount=10, to="alice")   # recorded; show the ticket with the call
# ... later, when the person answers (any process that opens the same record):
c4a.decide(ticket, "approve", by="sam")              # or "deny"

The ticket holds no arguments, only a random id and a signature. decide reads the call from the record, so nothing the client sends back can change what runs. A ticket the record did not issue, or one that was changed, expired or already decided, raises TicketRefused. The decision is stored with who made it. The action still runs only if it is called with the approved arguments, so a "deny" holds even if a framework runs the tool anyway.

With Pydantic AI (requires_approval=True tools):

from call4agents.adapters import pydantic_ai as c4a_pai

@agent.tool(requires_approval=True)
@c4a_pai.effect(approval=True)
def pay(ctx: RunContext, amount: int, to: str) -> str: ...

result = agent.run_sync("pay alice 10", conversation_id="order-42")   # ends with DeferredToolRequests
tickets = c4a_pai.tickets(result, [pay])                  # {tool_call_id: ticket}: show each with its call
results = c4a_pai.results({ticket: "approve"}, by="sam")  # the person's answers -> DeferredToolResults
agent.run_sync(message_history=result.all_messages(), deferred_tool_results=results,
               conversation_id="order-42")

With the OpenAI Agents SDK (needs_approval=True tools):

from call4agents.adapters import openai_agents as c4a_oa

pay_fn = c4a_oa.effect(pay, approval=True)                  # keep this one: tickets() needs it
agent = Agent(name="payer", tools=[function_tool(pay_fn, needs_approval=True)], ...)

result = await Runner.run(agent, "pay alice 10", context={"session_id": "order-42"})
tickets = c4a_oa.tickets(result, [pay_fn])                  # {call_id: ticket}
state = c4a_oa.apply(result.to_state(), {ticket: "approve"}, by="sam")   # state.approve / state.reject
await Runner.run(agent, state)

With LangGraph (the ticket goes in the interrupt; a node that re-runs on resume gets the same ticket back):

from call4agents.adapters import langgraph as c4a_lg

def ask(state, config):
    ticket = c4a_lg.pause(pay, config, **state["call"])
    interrupt({"call": state["call"], "ticket": ticket})

# when the person answers:
c4a.decide(ticket, "approve", by="sam")
graph.invoke(Command(resume="decided"), config)

Checks T1-T13 (python -m tests.test_tickets) cover a forged or edited ticket, a pause edited in the record, a ticket from another record, a second decision, expiry, a denied call that the framework runs anyway, and a call with other arguments than the approved ones. With the real frameworks they cover, for each of Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK and LangGraph: the approved call runs once, a denied call does not run, and a call that the client or the saved state changed after the pause does not run. (In the OpenAI Agents SDK, changed arguments under the same call id are already refused by the SDK itself; the check also covers a call replaced with a new id, which only the ticket catches.) Several machines (beta, new in 0.3)

Beta. Tested with separate processes and one local PostgreSQL server on Linux, macOS and Windows. Not yet used on real networks or in production; the options may still change.

When workers or replicas on different machines can pick up the same run, they need one shared record. Point every machine at the same PostgreSQL database and give them the same secret:

# pip install "call4agents[postgres]"
c4a.init("postgresql://user:password@db-host/agents", secret=os.environ["C4A_SECRET"].encode())

The table and the UNIQUE indexes are the same as in the SQLite file, so the same guarantees hold across machines. This covers the case in langgraph#7417, where a long tool call is sent to a second worker while the first is still running it. The second worker gets EffectInDoubt instead of running the call again, and a later caller gets the recorded result. The secret has to be passed in, because a local secret file would be different on each machine. The on-call commands take the address instead of a file: call4agents doubt postgresql://db-host/agents. Put the password in PGPASSWORD, not in the address, because command lines can be seen by other users. archive copies finished runs to a SQLite file and then removes them from the database. A crash between the two steps leaves those runs in both places; nothing is lost.

What is proven and what is not

Proven by tests in this repository (tests/):

  • the table above;
  • the big test (python -m tests.bigtest_c4a). 12 processes are killed at random while they charge 300 orders through a payment API that drops and delays answers. The result is 0 double charges. Without the kit, the same run charges 244 of 300 orders twice or more;
  • an action resumed in 3 new processes, as a method with a set argument, runs once;
  • a real process killed before and after every write to the record and inside the action, then the recovery killed too (python -m tests.test_crash_matrix, 412 crashes): no double charge and no unapproved payment;
  • call4agents crashtest finds the repeat in a small real agent on LangGraph, Pydantic AI and the OpenAI Agents SDK, and finds none with the guard (python -m tests.test_crashtest --require-frameworks); with our old approval bypass put back, its check fails;
  • 14 simultaneous callers of one action: it runs once;
  • 8 simultaneous actions on one "yes": exactly one runs;
  • 3,000 of 3,000 records from 20 parallel writers;
  • 5 kills during writes left the file intact;
  • a crash after a payment API charged, then a resume with the idempotency key: 1 charge, and the original charge is returned;
  • replay returns the same types, including real Pydantic and OpenAI SDK objects;
  • a shared PostgreSQL record (python -m tests.test_shared_record), with each machine played by a separate process: 8 machines call one action at once and it runs once; a long action still running on one machine is not started again by a second one; after a crash on one machine, the next raises EffectInDoubt; a "yes" given on one machine counts on another, only for the same arguments and the same secret.

Each guard is mutation-tested: when its bug is put back, its check fails. A no-op control is run next to every batch of mutations. Rerun them with python -m tests.mutations.run_kit_mutations.

  • real payment or email systems, and production traffic;
  • systems and Python versions not listed at the top of this page;
  • several real machines on a real network sharing one PostgreSQL record (the tests use separate processes and one local PostgreSQL server), and managed platforms such as LangGraph Cloud;
  • an independent code review (see docs/REVIEWED.md);

  • frameworks other than the four with adapters (LangGraph, Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP); the decorator itself works in any framework;

Costs and limits

  • A crash during an action is not resolved for you. You get EffectInDoubt unless you use reconcile= or idempotent_for=. Most frameworks would simply run the action again.
  • A refused approval means the action does not run. Your app has to ask the person again.
  • You decorate each action yourself, and call approve with the arguments the person saw.
  • Replaying a recorded run that contains approval-gated actions needs the approvals again in the new run record (c4a.approve(...) before the replayed call).
  • If the model rewrites the arguments on a retry (10 becomes 10.00), the call is treated as a new action. Pass c4a_key= (for example, an order id) when that can happen. A key names one action: calling it again with arguments that mean something else raises KeyConflict and nothing runs (numbers are compared by value, so 10, 10.0 and Decimal("10.00") are the same amount).
  • The secret in .c4a/secret protects approvals from anyone who cannot read that file. It does not protect them from someone who can (see docs/THREAT_MODEL.md).
